description: Defines recommendation logic that coaches use to match recipes to clients based on dimension score thresholds, meal plan templates, and substitution strategies.

ease_tier.label: Easy
ease_tier.description: Recipes that almost anyone can make successfully with minimal experience
ease_tier.coaching_note: These recipes build confidence. Encourage clients to master these first before moving up.

moderate_tier.label: Moderate
moderate_tier.description: Recipes that require some cooking experience but are still approachable
moderate_tier.coaching_note: Good for clients ready to expand their skills. Suggest pairing with an easy side to keep the total meal manageable.

challenging_tier.label: Challenging
challenging_tier.description: Recipes requiring solid cooking fundamentals and willingness to follow multi-step processes
challenging_tier.coaching_note: Reserve for motivated clients with a solid foundation. Plan these for weekends or meal-prep days when time pressure is low.

advanced_tier.label: Advanced
advanced_tier.description: Complex recipes for experienced cooks or highly motivated clients
advanced_tier.coaching_note: Only recommend to clients who have demonstrated competence at lower tiers. These are aspirational recipes that demonstrate growth.

weight_loss_quick_week.label: Weight Loss Quick Week
weight_loss_quick_week.description: Seven-day plan focused on high-satiety, low-calorie meals with minimal prep time

breakfast.dimension_notes: Prepare two breakfast options and rotate. Prioritize satiety and low sugar_profile.

lunch.dimension_notes: Batch-prep lunches. High health, high satiety. Leftover quality should be good.

dinner.dimension_notes: Three dinners that can be made in under 30 min. One-pan recipes preferred.

snack.dimension_notes: Low health score (meaning very healthy), minimal prep. Raw or assembled.

weight_loss_quick_week.prep_day_guidance: Sunday: batch-cook lunches and prep breakfast ingredients. Weeknights: quick assembly.

athlete_fueling_week.label: Athlete Fueling Week
athlete_fueling_week.description: Seven-day plan timed around training sessions with higher carb intake on training days

breakfast.dimension_notes: Moderate protein, high complex carbs. Quick to make on early training days.

pre_workout.dimension_notes: Easily digestible carbs. Low fat and fiber. Time_to_cook max 2.

post_workout.dimension_notes: Fast protein + carbs. Can be a shake or quick meal. Satiety 4-6.

dinner.dimension_notes: Balanced macros with higher carbs on training days. Good scalability.

athlete_fueling_week.prep_day_guidance: Sunday: prep protein and carb bases. Weekday post-workout meals should be 15 min or less.

beginner_cook_month.label: Beginner Cook Month
beginner_cook_month.description: Four-week progressive plan that builds cooking skills while maintaining nutritional quality

week_1.label: Confidence Building
week_1.focus: One-pan recipes with minimal steps. Build confidence and enjoyment.

week_2.label: Expanding Skills
week_2.focus: Introduce two-component meals (protein + side). Learn basic sauteing and roasting.

week_3.label: Building Complexity
week_3.focus: Three-component meals. Introduce sauces. Practice knife skills.

week_4.label: Consolidation
week_4.focus: Apply all learned skills. Attempt one challenging recipe. Plan a full meal.

beginner_cook_month.prep_day_guidance: Week 1: no prep needed. Week 2-4: introduce Sunday prep for 2-3ingredients.

heart_health_weekly.label: Heart Health Weekly
heart_health_weekly.description: Seven-day plan emphasizing low sodium, omega-3 rich foods, and fiber-dense meals

daily_targets.sodium_note: All recipes must score 1-3 on nutrition.sodium_level

breakfast.dimension_notes: Oat-based or egg-based. High fiber. Low sodium.

lunch.dimension_notes: Salad or soup-based. Lean protein. High micronutrient density.

dinner.dimension_notes: Fish 2x/week. Poultry or plant protein other nights. Steaming, poaching, baking preferred.

snack.dimension_notes: Nuts, fruit, low-fat yogurt. No processed snack foods.

heart_health_weekly.prep_day_guidance: Sunday: batch-cook grain bases and prep vegetable mise en place. Prepare fish on cooking day, not ahead.

meal_prep_sunday.label: Sunday Meal Prep
meal_prep_sunday.description: Single-day batch cooking session to produce meals for the entire work week

protein_base.dimension_notes: Large batch proteins (chicken breast, ground turkey, lentils). Yield 5+ servings each. Low cleanup.

grain_base.dimension_notes: Rice, quinoa, or pasta. Yield 5+ servings each. Pan-efficient.

vegetable_prep.dimension_notes: Roasted or steamed vegetables. Can be done in parallel with proteins. Sheet-pan preferred.

sauce_or_seasoning.dimension_notes: Versatile sauces that transform base proteins. Make once, use all week.

meal_prep_sunday.prep_day_guidance: Execute in order: start grains (longest passive time), then proteins, then sheet-pan vegetables, then sauces. Total active time target: 90 minutes. Cleanup target: under 30 minutes.

reduce_complexity.trigger: When steps > 5 for a client whose max is lower

strategies.strategy: Replace homemade sauce with quality pre-made sauce
Use pre-cut or frozen vegetables instead of hand-prepped
Replace multi-step breading with simple pan-sear
Convert multi-section recipe to simpler presentation (e.g., deconstructed)

improve_health.trigger: When nutrition score > 5 and goal requires nutrition_max <= 4

strategies.strategy: Swap refined grains for whole grains
Reduce sodium by half and add acid (lemon juice, vinegar) instead
Replace heavy cream with Greek yogurt or evaporated skim milk
Add extra vegetables to bulk up volume without adding calories
Reduce added sugar by 50% and add vanilla or cinnamon for perceived sweetness

reduce_time.trigger: When time_to_cook > 5 and client threshold is lower

strategies.strategy: Use pressure cooker or Instant Pot to convert slow-cook recipes
Batch-cook protein on Sunday and reheat throughout the week
Prep all mise en place the night before
Use sheet-pan method instead of multi-pot cooking
Choose faster-cooking protein (shrimp vs braised beef, chicken breast vs pork shoulder)

reduce_cleanup.trigger: When cleanup > 5 and client threshold is lower

strategies.strategy: Convert to one-pan or sheet-pan method
Use foil or parchment lining to eliminate scrubbing
Cook components sequentially in the same pan, wiping between
Choose recipes that use dishwasher-safe items only

conflict_resolution.description: When a client goal and a recipe's dimension scores conflict, use these resolution strategies

rules.conflict: Goal requires low time_to_cook but recipe is healthy and high-quality
rules.resolution: Recommend batch-prep or slow-cooker conversion. Suggest the client make it on a less busy day or prep components ahead.

rules.conflict: Goal requires easy recipes but client wants variety
rules.resolution: Use sauce rotations: prepare the same protein base with 2-3 different simple sauces. Same technique, different flavor.

rules.conflict: Goal requires low sodium but recipe relies on salt for flavor
rules.resolution: Substitute acid (lemon, lime, vinegar), umami (mushrooms, tomato paste, miso), herbs, and spices. Build flavor in layers.

rules.conflict: Goal requires weight loss but client reports hunger
rules.resolution: Shift toward higher-satiety recipes within the same caloric budget. Increase volume with low-calorie vegetables. Add protein to every meal.

rules.conflict: Goal requires meal prep efficiency but client finds batch cooking overwhelming
rules.resolution: Start with component prep (protein, grain, vegetable) rather than full-recipe batch cooking. Assemble fresh each day from prepped components.
